stem: In the library brief, why does LOAN deserve to be a class when 'fine' does not?
options: A loan is a relationship with its own facts (dates); a fine is just a CALCULATION on those facts
explanation: Nouns are candidates, not certainties. Loan owns BorrowedOn/DueOn/ReturnedOn; FineOn(date) is derived from them - a method, not a class.

stem: Why is DueDate on Book a design mistake?
options: A due date belongs to the RELATIONSHIP between member and book - lend it twice and Book has nowhere for two histories
explanation: When a fact belongs to a relationship rather than a thing, the relationship wants its own class. This is the workshop's central lesson.

stem: "A member may borrow up to 3 books" lives in Library, not Member, because:
options: Only the Library can SEE all of a member's open loans - the rule lives with the data it needs
explanation: The guiding question of the whole module: which object owns the data this rule needs? A rule far from its data is how code tangles.

stem: And "10p per day late" lives in Loan because:
options: The fine is computed from the loan's OWN dates - Loan.FineOn(date) uses nothing else
explanation: Same principle, opposite direction: this rule needs only DueOn and the query date, both Loan's own state.

stem: Return() printed "0 days late - fine £0.70". The cause?
options: The loan was CLOSED before DaysLateOn was read - and a closed loan correctly reports 0
explanation: Both numbers came from one loan and disagreed. When state changes alter what methods report, READ ORDER becomes logic: capture both values, then close.

stem: Borrow() starts with four early-return checks (unknown member, unknown book, unavailable, over limit). This style is:
options: Guard clauses - handle every bad case first, leaving the happy path unindented (1.5)
explanation: Each guard is one sentence of the brief, in order. The success path reads straight down with no nesting.

stem: Book.MarkLent() is internal and Library calls it. Why not let anyone set IsAvailable?
options: Availability must only change through a real loan - encapsulation (2.4) protecting the workflow
explanation: Book reports state; Library decides. A public setter would let code mark books lent with no loan existing.

stem: The workshop's own critique flags Library as weakening. Its suggested refactor?
options: Extract a LendingPolicy (max loans, loan length, fine rate) - Library is accumulating unrelated jobs
explanation: Stock + members + policy = cohesion dropping (2.13 S). Extracting policy gives rules one home and makes 'weekend rates' a one-class change.

stem: "The measure of a good model is not that it was right first time, but that ____"
explanation: First designs are never final. Localised rules, guarded state and loose coupling are what make the second draft affordable.

stem: Modelling the cinema (films, screens, showings, seats, bookings) - which fact belongs to SHOWING rather than Film?
explanation: Running time is the film's own; a start time only exists for a film-on-a-screen-at-a-moment - the Loan lesson again: relationship facts get relationship classes.
